text:
The Sharks have a first line now, and that changes how this season feels. Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith and Igor Chernyshov have generated 4.59 expected goals per 60 at 5v5 (expected goals measure the quality of chances) and win 62% of them, in a 64-minute sample that's small but loud. Add rookie Ivar Stenberg, already nominated for a Swedish award, and San Jose is selling something it hasn't had in years: a young core you can buy a ticket to see. Saturday's 4-3 win over Seattle had Celebrini losing his voice afterward.

The team numbers are still a rebuild's. San Jose is 11-12-2 with 44% of the expected goals, and it allows 3.77 expected goals per 60, a heavy load. The penalty kill gives up 0.96 expected goals a game. Goaltending has bailed it out by about nine and a half goals, while the shooters have finished about nine short of their chances, so the two roughly cancel. Our playoff odds are 9%.

The kids also show where the gaps are. Stenberg's line with Kiefer Sherwood and Michael Misa gets only 34% of the expected goals, and the Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring pair has been on for 6 goals for and 13 against at 5v5. Dmitry Orlov has 11 points in 10 games on 4.9 expected, running well ahead of his chances.

What we'd watch: how long the top line stays together, and whether the defence gets help.
